scope: Learner-facing progress and scheduling explanations, their in-app discovery, responsive and offline access, progress-adjacent Sync/backup boundaries, and the maintainer drift contract

statistics.note: Unique candidates only. Repair reopenings and repeated regression observations are verification history, not new found cases.

reopenObservations.reason: The first repair still lacked the concrete old-50-to-honest-0 explanation.
Progress itself still lacked a contextual guide link.
The mobile disclosure label hid sibling-guide navigation.
Equivalent Practice mutations still escaped the first token tripwire.
The guide misstated the extra-card trigger when a repeat cap excludes due cards.
Home still said nothing was due when a spent cap left a due backlog.
The recorded-Study completion screen still said nothing was due after the repeat cap excluded a due backlog.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: No public learner guide
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner sees a progress plateau but has no public explanation of grades, solid progress, exam mode, Practice, repeated misses, spread, or limits.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Baseline route inventory and learner journey

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Learner help was not discoverable from the app
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: First-run, Settings, About, and Progress could leave a learner without a direct route to the explanation.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Browser journeys from all four entry points

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: No canonical learner contract or deployment drift tripwire
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Observable scheduler behavior could change while learner prose stayed stale and deployment still succeeded.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Mobile documentation navigation was incomplete or misleading
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: At phone width a learner could not reliably discover every section or sibling guide.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Documentation pointed to stale Sync and deck-file locations
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner was sent to Progress for controls that live in Settings or About.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Learner documentation was not reliably available offline
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: An offline help navigation could fail or resolve to the app shell.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Offline navigation with cached app and docs

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: First-run help falsely promised that ordinary-review Hard returns within minutes
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A correct-but-slow established review can return after the displayed gap, potentially weeks.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Plain-language grade definitions were missing
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could grade by an attractive date instead of whether recall was wrong, slow, good, or immediate.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Learning and relearning behavior was undocumented
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could expect minute timers or one universal Hard path while queue positions and state steps behave differently.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Exam due-date projection and ordinary progress proof were not distinguished
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could mistake an earlier exam due date for lost or manufactured mastery.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Set, clear, reload, and midnight scenarios

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Exam introduction pacing and the zero-new pause were undocumented
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A future exam raises a non-zero daily value to fit the first 60% while zero remains an absolute pause.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The app falsely promised every card before an exam
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: More reviews can be due than the daily repeat limit serves.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Solid progress and the old synthetic 50% were not explained
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A fully seen 200-card course can honestly be 0% solid, while the old display manufactured exactly 50% from half-credit.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Known-well and three-weeks-later wording misdescribed earned future spacing
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The UI implied recall already demonstrated after three weeks while measuring an interval earned for the future.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Practice Ahead selection and non-recording behavior were undocumented
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could expect optional rehearsal to move dates, progress, totals, streaks, or achievements.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The repeated-miss filter looked like current weakness rather than lifetime history
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Three lifetime Again answers keep a recovered card flagged.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Interval spread and answer-scoped plan persistence were undocumented
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could not explain small date variation or know whether a revealed plan rerolls on reload or midnight.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The daily new setting was presented as a universal hard cap
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Exam mode can raise a non-zero value, and a section with an empty eligible queue after caps can add up to 20 recorded unseen cards even while due repeats wait outside the cap.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Exam pacing and cap-spent section-extra scenario

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Relearning Hard differs from new-card Hard
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A missed 30-day review retains about 12 days and normally leaves on its second uninterrupted Hard, not a new card's third Hard at one day.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Practice can include a due backlog and the repaired summary still denied it
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: With the daily repeat cap spent, all due cards enter Practice before the two capped optional additions, so neither Home nor the recorded-Study completion screen may claim nothing is due.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Excess repeats do not universally wait until tomorrow
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A card due only through an exam projection can stop being due when the exam becomes today.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The documentation drift gate overclaimed token checks as behavioral proof
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Practice batch or persistence semantics could change while the original tokens remained.
verificationHistory: fixed with probes and behavior tests

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Offline validation accepted the wrong Keep Club guide
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Creator HTML returned for the learner URL could pass generic docs markers.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Headerless portal bodies could be accepted as documentation assets
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A 200 response without Content-Type could populate CSS, SVG, or schema cache entries.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Visible progress vocabulary drifted between surfaces
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Browse used alternate terms for the four statuses used by Home and Progress.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The learner guide used undefined scheduler jargon
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A first-time learner had to infer internal terms such as ease and established review.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Narrow fragment targets hid beneath the wrapped sticky header
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: At 320px, a deep-linked heading landed partly under navigation.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Closed mobile navigation overlaid introductory content
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Links inside a closed disclosure remained laid over the page and interfered with hit testing.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Phone hit testing and keyboard disclosure

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Solid documentation omitted relearning precedence and one achievement contradicted it
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A lapsed card can retain 21+ days of proof but count as learning, while recovery copy called seven days solid.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Browse described cumulative misses as current slipping
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A fully recovered card was still called one that keeps slipping.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Long diagnostic codes widened phone documentation
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Generated error terms pushed the page beyond a 320px viewport.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Unseen Practice Hard does not retain temporary learning steps
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Every answer uses a fresh temporary record, so repeated Hard never reaches recorded Study's three-Hard exit.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: A draft audit artifact persisted the supplied Sync capability
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A secret included in the user report could have been committed with the audit.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Main-loop source and temporary-snapshot scan without emitting the value

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The final reviewed product lacked a reproducible manifest digest
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A critic could not prove which moving-tree bytes the verdict reviewed.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Audit artifacts lacked a canonical registry and reconciled statistics
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Findings, refutations, reopenings, and open contexts could not be independently recounted.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Recorded defaults were incorrectly labelled by-design decisions
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: An unnamed RECORDED context could suppress a future finding despite no RULING-grade decision.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Persisted audit evidence anchors were stale or misattributed
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A reviewer following an exact candidate, kill-list, or test pointer could land on a blank, unrelated statement, nonexistent symbol, or a suite that did not make the claimed assertion.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Independent line/symbol follow-through and deploy-test assertion inventory
verificationHistory: main-loop anchor correction and machine/report alignment

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: A same-build service-worker install could overwrite the active shell before validation
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Reusing the same cache name let a failed install damage an already complete offline generation.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Same-stamp portal substitution with existing complete cache

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Correct-MIME impostor bodies could poison documentation assets
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Portal content labelled text/css, image/svg+xml, or application/json passed type-only validation.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Settings understated the scope of a Sync key
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could share a key believing it covered one deck although the capability covers synced data for every built-in course using it.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Local-deck backup copy implied migration or disaster recovery it cannot provide
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A reimported deck receives a new local identity, so the old backup cannot move its review history to another browser or phone.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Backup stamp and wrong-deck restore path

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The guide called a rounded month/year label an exact displayed interval
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A stored 38-day plan is shown as one month even though the exact underlying day count remains 38.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Generic Easy copy was false during learning and relearning
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Good and Easy can graduate to the same retained gap there, and Easy does not raise ease.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Exam-cap prose omitted the historical schedule-origin anchor
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Enabling an exam later projects an existing interval from its answer date and can make a card immediately due.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Older answer made immediately due by a new exam

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Local progress copy said device where the real boundary is a browser profile and origin
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Two browsers on one phone do not share IndexedDB, Cache Storage, or localStorage.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Storage implementation and all learner-copy surfaces

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Imported-review achievement wording did not match its metric
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The rule counts all recorded answers in any local deck, including first presentations and self-created decks.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Achievement context and exact catalog copy

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Local-deck help denied or hid the separate card export
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A learner could believe no file carries a self-made deck even though Settings offers Deck file, while Backup serves a different purpose.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The guide omitted that another Again resets relearning to step zero
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: After Again then another Again, three uninterrupted Hards are needed rather than two.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Again, Again, Hard, Hard, Hard sequence

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Minimum one-day variation falsely implied the result must change
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The spread extends a day each way but its center bucket can return the unchanged interval.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Low, midpoint, and high deterministic rolls

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Lunch achievement copy claimed memory retention from any answer event
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The hour-based rule unlocks even on Again, so kept a memory was unsupported.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: The repaired app still uses standard Anki or FSRS scheduling
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Scheduler and import documentation would misidentify the algorithm or preserve Anki history.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: A merely seen card still receives half progress
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The repaired 200-card all-young fixture would show a non-zero solid percentage.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Exam mode still overwrites ordinary mastery proof
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Set/clear or sync grouping would mutate the canonical ordinary schedule or proof.
candidateRegistry.handRepro: Set, clear, reload, and merge grouping

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Practice mutates durable scheduling, totals, streaks, or achievements
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: A complete Practice round would alter durable progress facts.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Repeated-miss represents current weakness and clears after recovery
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Later Good/Easy answers would remove the cumulative marker.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: A revealed interval rerolls after reload or midnight
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: The interval pressed after restore would differ from the plan revealed before it.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Offline learner help can resolve to the app, another guide, or a portal
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Route or asset substitution would be accepted into the current offline shell.

candidateRegistry.bareClaim: Keyboard users cannot skip repeated navigation or operate mobile docs navigation
candidateRegistry.failureScenario: Skip links or disclosure focus would fail under keyboard-only use.
